mission.title: Confession
mission.description: Terminate the corrupted Hypatia, then bring the intruder to his meeting with the Architect.

npc.say: Just tell them I'll be there.
It is the duty of a program to serve the system that created it.

phase.briefing:
Greetings...operative. We appear to have succeeded in reaching the intruder and drawing his rampage to a close. However, damaged areas of the simulation remain.
One problem that has come to our attention is the Exile librarian, Hypatia. Terminated by the intruder when she failed to deliver what he requested of her, she was restored by her supporters, but imperfectly: the intruder's override code still infects her system.
In order to correct this glitch, Hypatia must be terminated...again.

enter.say:
Dude, did you hear about the intruder killing Gray? I guess Gray managed to get him to talk, but the intruder took something the wrong way, and... And then Pace came and talked to him, and managed not to get herself killed.
Anyway, I know they can restore Agents when they die and all that, but what the intruder does to programs isn't exactly normal...as I guess we're about to see for ourselves with Hypatia. Let's see...
That's where she's supposed to be. I've got unregistered programs in there--probably her Bookwyrms.

done.say: Phew. Now, I just hope Gray doesn't turn out to have white sparks radiating off his head, too...

phase.briefing: Operative, Agent Pace was able to obtain the intruder's consent to meet with the Architect concerning his...problem. This meeting is now imminent. Please approach the intruder and notify him.

enter.say: Looks like he's in there, all right.

talk.say: All right. I assume they know what will happen if they try lying to me again.

phase.briefing: I think it will be useful if we confer briefly before the meeting takes place, {player}.

enter.say: Huh. Wonder what this is about.

talk.say:
We did...mislead the intruder before he entered the Matrix. This was done in an attempt to convince him that there was no need for him to enter the System, as it was clear that his presence would present many dangers.
We now find ourselves forced to tell him the truth, again in the hope of preventing his presence within the Matrix. If this fails as well, then the situation will be grave indeed.

done.say: We are...constrained to certain courses of action, operative. The System must be preserved.

talk.say: I am counting on you to be prepared for any eventuality, tesoro. As programs, we are at a great disadvantage when facing the intruder's override codes.

done.say:
The intruder has already shown that he will not hesitate to terminate us. Agent Gray was restored at great cost. I was fortunate that I was able to...persuade the intruder to listen to reason.
I...do not want to be terminated, {player}.

phase.briefing: Proceed to the meeting place, operative. We will be assembling there shortly.

talk.say:
No more stalling. I know it exists.
Give me the biological interface program!

You are correct to posit the program's existence. However, we did not create it. There is only one extant copy: the one that was removed from this simulation--the one that you yourself detected outside of the System.

done.say: There appears to be no immediate danger from the intruder, operative. We will discuss this outcome in more detail on a private channel.
Thank you, operative. That will be all.

...
Damn and blast these useless programs...

mission.finish: As logic alone does not direct the intruder, his next move cannot be predicted with absolute certainty...but if he is, in fact, convinced that the object of his search is not here, he should leave the System, and we will be able to restore the simulation to its optimal state.
